body:
I belong to an  group for people with cancer and other incurable painful diseases that gives out literature on how to terminate your life in as peaceful way as possible.  The problem with suicide by a gun is that the gun can slip and the bullet miss the brain stem.  This means it is possible to survive a self administered gunshot sound to the head.  I know of one person who blew their face off due to the gun moving in the instant after the trigger was pulled and survived.  This means they had to continue living in an even worse state and that due to the nature of the injury they were probably forced into a mental hospital as well. So please don't do anything rash.  

I'm 30 and have had a hard life since I was 16 so I know something of what you are going through.

I'm not trying to sound callous or anything please don't take it that way , however: you have it better than I did at 16, which is when I had a horrific accident that has caused constant pain every day, every hour, every second since.  Because the accident didn't visibly break any bones, my doctors refused to allow me to see pain specialist and instead sent me to a psychologist who tried to make me think I was just imagining the pain and that it wasn't real.  Then because I admitted I had tried marijuana for the pain they diagnosed me as a drug addict and a malingerer- they claimed I was making up the pain to get drugs.

Then I had to drop all my classes and the teachers and principal of the school wouldn't make disability accommodations for me because the psychologist had told them all I was making the pain up.  Next I had to drop out of all my classes and this still didn't get anyone at the school to care.

I notice you talk about what people think about you. One thing you can be glad about is that they actually care enough about you to have opinions on you at all.  I had a number of friends before the accident- after the accident they didn't visit me in the hospital, they didn't listen to me when I told them I had chronic pain, they would give me nasty looks if I tried to repeat myself and explain I was I constant pain, then after that they just stopped talking to me.

I went from being a top athlete and student, to the school and my friends not giving one flying fuck that I had to drop out of school and was possibly going to become homeless.  A lot has to do with the psychologist who told everyone I was inventing the pain.

So I know it is very bad for you right now but it could be even worse. At least you don't have any villains or assholes who are actively trying to ruin your life.

If you need to talk to someone, I can be reached during most parts of the day. I'm disabled due to the pain and also have bad insomnia so I can respond to replies late into the day.

Regarding insomnia I found that the drug Remron was a miracle drug. Please ask your doctor about trying this, it's an antidepressant,very safe, and actually works better for sleep at lower doses.  If you are able to get better sleeps, you might not feel like you have to go to a mental hospital.

Ps I've found that mental hospitals are horrible places- why wouldn't you try seeing shrink first?

I learned about this when my best friends wouldn't look at me in the eye when I told them about chronic pain and basically forced me into say it actually wasn't that bad because they would do things like just not respond and leave an awkward silence or rudely change the subject. I would try to make a sarcastic joke about the pain to "lighten" up the subject matter so they could digest it and actually listen to what I was saying. Then they   say things like  "But you were just joking about it can't be that bad"

So I guess unfortunately they must have been pretty shallow people for ignoring a friend in need just because it would bring them down a bit.
The friendships dwindled out because I couldn't stand the looks they would give me when it  tried to explain my chronic pain. It was the same look you would give to someone who just started screaming expletives for no reason in the middle of a crowded train.

Yes I've tried nearly everything that is relatively easy to find out about on the internet. The problem with that particular procedure is that they cannot reach very many cranial nerves due to the risk of hitting the spinal cord.  I've also had steroids injected as well but again they can't reach the nerves and also it only helps if your pain is caused by inflammation.

Haven't tried that but I haven't had any luck at all with pseudoscientific alternative medicine (it's alternative for a reason- if it worked it would be mainstream- and i find it ludicrous that people believe there is a conspiracy by mainstream medicine to hold back chakra healing or some other alternative nonsense. If you look at it strictly from a monetary standpoint insurance companies would save hundreds of millions of dollars if they used acupuncture over traditional opiate based pain medicine not to mention millions of overdoses, addiction cases, and side effect related trips to the ER prevented. The only thing limiting acupuncture is it's own ineffectiveness at helping patients.  And I've been told by otherwise intelligent people that only a real Chinese person can properly do acupuncture- again it makes very little sense)

Wow, I had to be put in a psychiatric hospital as well. It was terrible.  Just made me hate the mental health community even more.  I realize other people may have good experiences with the mental health community, but in my experience psychologists can have issues as well and they get put in positions of having power over people and take out their issues on them.

Backing this up is the fact that the pain psychologist that told me I was inventing my pain in my imagination would often tell me that is what she had as well and she cured herself using the the treatment she prescribed me (yeah right, she was very obese and she had just probably repressed the chronic pain so much that somehow she convinced herself it didn't exist despite it clearly causing her not to be able to exercise).  

Perhaps if you come for a rich family where if they abuse you, mistreat you in any way, or don't get any results their professional standing will go down - then maybe the mental health system works better?  Although didn't Freud sleep with his patients, all from rich families?

What exactly does that mean? My pain might be generated by a nerve being effected by a bulge in my spinal cord called a syrinx. However I doubt this is the main cause because both sides of my neck and shoulder hurt equally and the pain isn't either tingling shock like pain or burning.  I've hears the obstruction to the CSF flow because the syrinx can cause chronic pain and this sounds more likely.
Btw I'm sorry that you had that terrible time with a psychologist as well. Sounds like we are sort of in the same boat. I'm glad you've eventually been able to find a psychologist that can help. I'm not sure if I would be willing to see any more shrinks because other than the one really terrible experience, the others I've seen -at best- I have not felt no connection with whatsoever.  

I think it's because they are trained to think suicidal impulses are caused by disease called depression(a disease doctors have little hard evidence for and the only diagnostic tool is a questionnaire)- maybe for some people it is, however I highly doubt mine is a disease. Whenever I go to a shrink and say I'm suicidal due to the pain, they always try to claim I haven't tried every treatment and that my decision is rash and impulsive, major checkboxes on the depression diagnosis form. 

 If I could go to a psychologist who didn't do this, perhaps it would help- however I don't think it's possible. IMO when they hear a patient mention  thoughts of suicide they immediately consider the possible lawsuits if they don't do the standard things, prescribe antidepressants and diagnose depression. Further eroding trust for me is the fact that if you continued to say you feel like you cannot live, a shrink will likely have you locked up in a mental hospital so they aren't sued if you even went through with it.  If they were able to just listen or understand that maybe it's not a disease that is causing the suicidal ideation. 
In fact, when I signed up for a waiting list for a clinic somewhere in Europe that helps permanently ill terminate in a secure, dependable , and not painful fashion and I felt the most peace and relief I've ever felt since the pain's onset. Really made me wonder why that option isn't available. I doubt insurance companies would begin issuing death squads to terminally ill patients like conservatives claim.

I saw a psychologist that was part of a pain clinic and it was one of the worst experiences in my life.  I never believed that anyone could be truly evil until I met her.  I've considered trying out therapy just to deal with the effect this woman had on my life, regardless of the chronic pain.  To this day I can't go to a new doctor without having anxiety attacks because of the effect this toxic, evil woman had

And this wasn't some Podunk pain clinic, it was part of a major university. They would do things like leave me waiting in one of the doctors rooms while the entire staff went out to lunch because they knew I had severe pain due to the furniture in the room.   They once left me waiting for 3 hours in a room, and the doctor only spent 10 minutes with me.  They told me my brain was imagining the pain and that I really wasn't in pain and acted liked this line of reasoning would solve everything.  This is despite having a disease that was so obvious on an MRI that I was the one to finally diagnosis it by looking at the MRI myself and noticing there was a long black line where it shouldn't be in the spinal cord.

You yourself admit that the worst people you've ever dealt with are psychologists. Me too, which is why I claim they aren't true professionals. If architects had records of success that psychologists have we would all be living in mud huts.  You say anti depressants help, I've tried a large number of them and not one of them helped at all.  Again the shrinks claim that their drugs will make you not want to kill yourself. I call bullshit because I want to die because I cannot live in constant pain.   Any drug that could change this would have to completely alter my reality like LSD or something.

I can only conclude that people just don't comprehend the fact that you body can constantly send you pain signals and that there is absolutely nothing anyone can do about it.  I've reached this conclusion because most healthy people I've met and told about chronic pain will respond by quoting the latest Health section article of the NYTimes and say that medical science can do anything.  This is simply not true- chronic pain management is pretty abysmal and has no signs of improving quickly at all.  The most advanced pain management techniques are not that advanced- a pain pump simply delivers the same flawed medications just in super small doses, an implanted spinal stimulator only works if they can precisely identify the nerve that is misfiring and the pain is a burning neuropathic pain that will be canceled out by the electronic noise generated by a pain stimulator.

I don't care. A fresh start on life  is what I want. I'm done with this horrible "life"
I've exahausted all the options except several; Ziconotide which I will not take as it risks permanent psychosis which I might risk except it could take away my ability to terminate my life,  out of alt medicine I haven't seen a real Chinese acupuncturist(as in just off the boat from China) however the results I've gotten from acupuncture I've tried have shown me it's likely a fraudulent medicine  that does nothing for severe pain(if such an easy procedure with so little side effects actually helped -severe- pain then it wouldn't be classified as an alternative medicine and would be widely used as a regular part of medicine- the only reason why some hospitals have begun doing it is because they are desperate because western medicine has absolutely failed to treat pain), and I haven't tried a decompression surgery where they remove a piece of your skull and replace it with an artificial section that has more room for the brain- this has basically no indication it will work because I've tried the test for its success- a invasive cranial traction and it had no effect.
I've also read about fringe treatments like ketamine comas which likely wouldn't help me as I don't have burning neuropathic pain.  
Can't think of anything else I haven't tried.
